# Device-related infections

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Infectious diseases > Wound, soft tissue, bone, and joint infections > Device-related infections*

[Original Article Link](/library/0s0eth)

---

## Summary

Device-related infections are associated with surgical implants, e.g., pacemakers or <u>joint</u> prostheses. Clinical presentation ranges from asymptomatic infections resulting from device <u>erosion</u>, to severe systemic illness, <u>sepsis</u>, and <u>septic shock</u>. Diagnosis is generally clinical, supported by laboratory and imaging studies and intraoperative evidence of infection. Diagnosis is confirmed by microorganism growth in cultures taken from or near the device, or by evidence of infection on <u>biopsy</u> samples. Management is multidisciplinary, with assistance from surgical teams and infectious disease services, and it includes <u>antibiotic therapy</u> and invasive treatment of the device (usually removal).




This article provides an overview of the diagnosis and management of common device-related infections. See also “<u>Intravascular catheter-related bloodstream infections</u>” and “<u>Hospital-acquired infections</u>.”
